findings.text: 200 m+ silhouette fails on value separation and on subject. From 240 m out the region is a flat grey-green gravel pan against a pale cyan sky with almost no value range; the strongest silhouette anywhere in a sunken frame is the neighbouring Void's floating isles. There is no landmark read and no staircase read from the approach — the Court only becomes visible at ~140 m, and then only as a small ruin island.

findings.text: Night has no light source in the region at all. A 'drowned court' at 23:00 is completely unlit — no lanterns, no aether glow, no reflected light on the water from the ruin. The sky and aurora carry the frame alone. (The night sky grade itself is the best-looking thing in the region.)
findings.evidence: tools/out/crit6-sunken-b/shot-night-in.png

findings.text: Regression gate NOT RUN and therefore not passed: 'node tools/gate.mjs' refused to start ('8 chrome-headless-shell process(es) are already running') because of GPU contention from the parallel critic fleet. I did not force it and did not kill other agents' processes. What I can report from direct observation instead: no washed-white blob appeared in any of ~60 frames including a full fight with drowned + wisp + leviathan (impacts render as saturated purple/magenta with hue intact), collision held while walking, and the wading drag works (walk speed dropped 6.6 -> 3.63 m/s in the flooded plaza).
findings.evidence: gate stdout: '[gate] ==== NOT STARTING ==== 8 chrome-headless-shell process(es) are already running.'; crit6-sunken-b/burst-fight-*.png and burst-levi-fight-*.png (no white-out); crit6-sunken-c report.json state() after 5 s of held W: speed 3.63, grounded true.

regions.biggestGap: The Void has one good photograph in it — the 120-240 m walk-in, where the broken ring, the isles and the violet dissolve compose into something no other region has — and then it fails every acceptance distance around that photograph: combat still repaints the region amber (up to 53% of the frame, driven by the Void's OWN void-element bestiary while the player never fires, because the impact presets in src/vfx/VFX.js hard-code gold/orange regardless of element), the 130 m abyss that is the region's premise is still invisible from its own rim for the third wave running, and at 8 m the hero landmark is untextured flat facets with neon-tape conduits. A player off Destiny 2 and FF14 would like the skyline for ten seconds and then find nothing underneath it.

findings.text: COMBAT STILL REPAINTS THE VOID AMBER — wave 5's finding, un-fixed in kind. Not white any more, but the region's identity is still erased by its own bestiary. Root cause is element-blind warm presets in src/vfx/VFX.js: lines ~672 (color(0xffd070, 0xffa040)), ~683 (0xe89a20, 0xff9040), ~684 (0xffcf5a, 0xff8030) and ~690 (c0 always 0xffcf5a) hard-code gold/orange for impacts regardless of def.projectile.element, so a void bolt landing throws solar sparks.
findings.evidence: VC-C/burst-approach-5.png: player never fired (HUD reads 6/60 all run, god+passive off only for the enemies), 52.8% of the frame measured warm (r > b+18, r > 70), mean warm rgb (173,103,95); the ring, the isles and the crystals are bleached behind an orange gradient. Reproduced clean in VC-D with ONLY void-element enemies alive (eval returned Void Horror / Riftling / Fen Wraith, all element 'void', no player fire step in the script): burst-a-7/8/9 measure 18.2%/21.6%/18.2% warm and the sky's whole upper-left quadrant goes tan (VC-D/burst-a-8.png).
findings.failure_scenario: Walk into the Void at noon, let a riftling and a voidhorror open on you without firing back; within 3 s the violet sky and the landmark are behind an orange-tan wash covering a fifth to a half of the screen.

findings.text: THE 130 M ABYSS IS STILL INVISIBLE FROM ITS OWN RIM — wave-4's blocker verbatim, now unfixed for three waves. The drop that the whole region is built on (heightAt goes 49.4 at r=115 to -82.7 at r=135, measured in-engine) has no lip, no cliff face, no strata, no rim light, no depth grading. Standing on it you read a gentle dark slope and walk off.
findings.evidence: VC-E/shot-rim-out.png (player at [-453.6, 49.3, -453.6], i.e. 3 m from the edge, pitch -0.12): the ground simply continues to frame bottom, no edge is visible anywhere. VC-E/shot-rim-down.png at pitch -0.42: the lower half is an unlit near-black smear in which floor and wall are indistinguishable. Confirmed by the harness itself — in VC-C the player went from y≈45 to y=-11.59 mid-fight with no traversal input, and in VC-E spawnNear dropped a Riftling to y=-2.3 and a Void Horror to y=4.63 while the ground was at 49.

findings.text: THE MOUNTAIN RING IS STILL CRISP AND FULLY READABLE INSIDE THE VOID AT NOON — also verbatim from waves 4 and 5. The region's stated premise (fogMul 5.0, skyVeil 0.84, 'the horizon LINE stops existing') does not survive contact: from the heart the ring fills the frame at high contrast with its tan scree and snow streaks legible, merely tinted purple. The Void reads as a purple valley with big purple mountains, which is generic fantasy, not 'reality gave up here'.
findings.evidence: VC-B/shot-tod13-out.png (standing at (-622,-622), noon, looking outward): the ring occupies the top two thirds at full detail with pale streaks resolved. Same failure at 8 m from the landmark, VC-A/shot-lm-8-side.png top-left. Same again from the rim, VC-E/shot-rim-out.png, where both flanking ranges and the pass saddle are sharp.
findings.failure_scenario: Stand anywhere in the Void at hour 13 and look away from the landmark; the world you were told dissolved is fully present and sharply lit.

findings.text: THE BORDER IS AN ATMOSPHERE SWITCH, NOT A JOURNEY. Cross into the Sunken Kingdom and the Void's fog does not fall off — it stops. Looking back from ~120 m outside, the Void has bright pale-blue daylight sky, its isles hang in perfectly clear air, and its ground reads ordinary grey-green rock. From the other side, at 240 m on the walk-in, green Vale trees sit inside the violet grade with no transition at all.
findings.evidence: VC-B/shot-bx-2-back.png (biomeAt returned 'sunken' at (-647,-301), camera turned back toward the Void): daylight sky, zero haze on the isles, purple crystals reading as pasted-on props. VC-B evals: 'void' at (-592,-419), 'sunken' at (-647,-301) — the swap happens over one step. VC-E/shot-walkin-240.png: green canopy at the right edge inside the violet grade.
findings.failure_scenario: Walk out of the Void toward the Sunken Kingdom and turn around: the region you just left is lit like a normal afternoon and its skyline is a set of props in clear air.

findings.text: THE LANDMARK FAILS THE 8 M TEST. The Unmaking's drum, courses and dentils are huge flat facets carrying one stretched low-frequency noise — no veining, no dirt, no chipping, no bevels, no secondary carving. The 'conduit still burning inside the wound' and the fragment lights are flat uniform magenta strips that read as glow-tape stuck on rock. There is also a dashed hairline black polygon sliver rendering across empty sky right beside it.
findings.evidence: VC-A/shot-lm-8.png and the 2x crop VC-A/_sliver.png: the drifting fragments are plain untextured boxes with hard flat faces; the magenta bar bottom-right is a solid rounded strip with no falloff into the stone; the dashed black line at top-left is a zero-thickness polygon in open sky. VC-A/shot-lm-40.png shows the same at 40 m — the ornament hierarchy is one dentil band and nothing else.
findings.failure_scenario: Walk up to the hero landmark and look at the stone; there is nothing there to look at, and a rendering sliver is visible beside it.

findings.text: SHIELD BUBBLES WASH OUT EVERY VOID CREATURE. Riftling and Void Horror both spawn inside a hard-edged, low-poly translucent egg roughly twice the body's width, with no fresnel rim, no hex/scale pattern and no animation. Against the violet sky it becomes the palest element in the frame and greys the creature inside into an unreadable tangle; the ellipse's faceted silhouette is visible on its outline.
findings.evidence: VC-C/_z2.png (crop of shot-fight-t3.png, voidhorror at ~18 m): a milky lavender egg with polygon-edged outline, the robed body desaturated to grey behind it. VC-E/shot-creat-near.png: at 20 m the creature is an indistinct dark blob inside a pale oval. Compare Destiny 2, where a shield is tighter than the body, saturated, patterned and animated.
findings.failure_scenario: Any shielded Void encounter: you cannot tell what you are shooting at, and the brightest thing on screen is the shield, not the creature.

findings.text: THE VOID HAS NO SKY EVENT AT ANY HOUR. Noon is a flat violet gradient with one blurred cloud band and no sun. Golden hour is the same frame hue-rotated pink — no raking light, no long shadows, no warm rim on the isles' undersides. Night is near-black with essentially no stars, no aurora, and crystals that emit no light onto the ground. Against FF14's dramatic skies with god rays this is an empty backdrop at all three times.
findings.evidence: VC-B/shot-tod13-sky.png (noon), shot-tod17-lm.png (17.5), shot-tod23-lm.png (23) from the same camera at (-622,-622). Night has the region's only genuinely good look but zero readability — a player fighting there would see nothing.

regions.biggestGap: The Vale is a grassland whose grass only exists in a ~25 m bubble that follows the camera. Past a hard, dead-straight LOD line the "meadow" is a bald flat green plane with no ground cover at all, and every tree, rock, enemy, cottage and the Aetheryte plaza itself stands on that bald plane — it is in literally every settled screenshot I took (8 s of settle time, so this is not pop-in). Layered on top: the 200 m and 8 m acceptance distances both fail. At 200 m the mountain ring dissolves into a flat white sawtooth with zero value separation from the haze and the Aetheryte is invisible; at 2-8 m the hero landmark's gold is a smooth untextured plastic tube, boulders are faceted lumps, the mountain-ring cliff is one stretched rock photo on a flat plane, cottages are boxes with painted-on timbers, and the Sundered Spire — a RUIN — still stands on an immaculate polished cream marble plaza with clean joints and gold vein lines, which is the wave-4 blocker verbatim, third wave running. Wave 6 did land real things here (no combat white-out, a sculpted-faced villager, an ornamented Aetheryte at 40 m, a working hamlet and border read), but a player off FF14 would clock this as an in-progress hobby project within ten seconds of looking at the ground or at any surface within arm's reach.

findings.text: THE GRASS ONLY EXISTS IN A ~25 m BUBBLE AROUND THE CAMERA, AND THE EDGE IS A HARD LINE. The Vale is the grass biome and its grass stops dead at roughly 25-28 m in a straight arc across the frame; beyond it the entire meadow out to the treeline is a flat, bald, untextured green plane. This is not pop-in — I teleported, waited 8 full seconds, and shot it. Every tree, boulder, cottage, market stall, enemy and the Aetheryte plaza itself stands on bald ground. FF14's Central Shroud and Destiny's EDZ hold ground cover to 60-100 m with a soft fade; here the boundary is visible, geometric and it slides along with you as you walk. This single fact undoes the one thing wave 5's critic praised (the grass shader inside 25 m).
findings.evidence: tools/out/V6-F/shot-hamlet-wide.png (dense blades stop in a hard line at ~y=580, bald green plane above it to the horizon); tools/out/V6-G/burst-atk-3.png (the Aether Hound stands on the bald plane, grass edge running the full width at ~y=560); tools/out/V6-A/shot-spire-200.png; tools/out/V6-C/shot-grass-forward-settled.png

findings.text: THE SUNDERED SPIRE IS STILL A RUIN ON A PRISTINE POLISHED MARBLE PLAZA — the wave-4 blocker, unchanged, third wave running. Clean 2-3 m cream tiles with sharp joints and gold filigree vein lines, zero cracks, zero missing tiles, zero rubble, zero weeds, zero dirt, zero wear. The ruin above it is one running-bond brick photo at one scale on the arch voussoirs (which should be radial wedges), the column drums, the tower and the floor slabs alike, with plain box capitals and square window holes. Interior slabs float with no support and wear the same brick on their undersides.
findings.evidence: tools/out/V6-A/shot-spire-45.png, tools/out/V6-A/shot-spire-12.png

findings.text: MATERIAL TRUTH FAILS AT 2-8 m ON EVERY HERO SURFACE. The Aetheryte's gold — the game's front door, at 1 m — is a perfectly smooth extruded tube with a soft plastic-yellow gradient and a blown-out white highlight: no chasing, no engraving, no bevel, no darkened recesses, no anisotropy, no grime, and the tube ends are cut flat and float. The mountain-ring cliff at 8 m is one grey rock photo stretched and vertically smeared across a flat plane with no ledges, strata or boulders. The Mirrormere boulder at 2 m is a smooth faceted purple lump with a speckle texture and no cracks, lichen or chipped edges. Cottage plaster is a flat plane with low-frequency mottling and the half-timbering is a flat black stripe with zero thickness. None of this survives a blind cut against FF14, where the same objects carry carving, bevels and dirt at that range.
findings.evidence: tools/out/V6-D/burst-sprintgrass-3.png (Aetheryte gold spiral at ~1 m); tools/out/V6-D/shot-border-r400.png (cliff face); tools/out/V6-F/shot-lake-settled.png (boulder, right of frame); tools/out/V6-A/shot-hamlet-8.png (plaster + timbers)

findings.text: AT 200 m THERE IS NO SILHOUETTE AND NO VALUE SEPARATION. The mountain ring reads as a flat near-white cut-out with a jaggy triangular sawtooth edge sitting on a pale blue sky — the ring and the sky are the same value, so the world's horizon simply disappears. Worse, the region's own landmark is INVISIBLE from 208 m: no beacon, no light shaft, no crystal read. FF14 aetherytes anchor a whole zone from any ridge; Destiny landmarks read as silhouettes from a kilometre. This is one third of the acceptance rule failing outright.
findings.evidence: tools/out/V6-D/shot-noon-sky.png (white-on-white sawtooth ring at y≈520-620); tools/out/V6-A/shot-aeth-200.png (Aetheryte not findable in frame from z=180)

findings.text: THE GATE'S OWN BLOB TEST FAILS IN THE SPAWN MEADOW DURING ORDINARY COMBAT. `python tools/blobcheck.py tools/out/V6-C` returns BLOBCHECK FAIL with five flashing ground-cover clusters. The source is the Dawnbreak Verdict viewmodel's front sight posts: they are white-clipped flat tips that bloom a halo onto the grass behind them, and the halo flickers frame to frame. The clusters keep a green hue (mean rgb 117,144,63 / 120,153,62 / 84,148,60) so this is NOT the washed-white decree violation — but the sight posts themselves are a small element that tone-maps to white instead of a hue, and per CLAUDE.md any gate failure is an automatic LOSE.
findings.evidence: blobcheck output: FLASHING BLOB burst-fight-1 vs -0 (10 px at [740,381]); -3 vs -2 (21 px at [737,377]); -6 vs -5; -8 vs -7 (4 clusters); burst-fight2-1 vs -0. Zoomed source: tools/out/V6-C/burst-fight-3.png at 1920-space (1474,754) is the gun's white sight blades with a glow halo.

findings.text: ENEMY NAMEPLATES ARE ANCHORED ~300 px ABOVE THE CREATURE, floating in open sky with a full health bar and no connection to the body. At 30 m the Aether Hound sits at y≈500 and its plate sits at y≈180. In one frame the plate labelled the wrong entity entirely (a stationary wisp crystal carried an 'Aether Hound' plate). Destiny and FF14 both pin the plate to the head; this reads as a broken HUD projection.
findings.evidence: tools/out/V6-G/burst-atk-1.png and burst-atk-3.png; mislabelled plate in tools/out/V6-E/burst-charge-4.png

findings.text: THE HAMLET IS STILL A GREYBOX VILLAGE. Every cottage is the same rectangular prism with a pyramid roof at the same scale: flat plaster planes, half-timbering painted on as flat black stripes with no relief, a brick plinth strip, one square window hole with a brick surround set into plaster (wrong material logic), and on several faces no door at all. The well is a black cube with a grey blob in it. The market stall's canopy is a single tilted plank quad hovering with a long unsupported overhang that clips into the cottage roof behind it. Benches and posts are untextured black planks. Grass grows straight through the plank decking, the market counter and the raised garden beds. FF14's Bentbranch or Destiny's Cosmodrome outbuildings are not in the same category.
findings.evidence: tools/out/V6-A/shot-hamlet-8.png, tools/out/V6-D/shot-hamlet-settled.png (grass through decking bottom-right; floating red canopy left of centre)

findings.text: ONE BRICK PHOTO IS DOING ALL THE MASONRY IN THE REGION, at one scale, on things that are not the same material: the Sundered Spire's arches and floor slabs, the hamlet field walls, the cottage plinths, the vegetable-bed edging and the loose paving strips. On the field wall each brick reads about 30 cm tall. Wave 5 called this out verbatim and it is untouched.
findings.evidence: tools/out/V6-C/burst-villager-2.png (field wall brick scale), tools/out/V6-E/shot-villager.png (identical brick on the garden beds), tools/out/V6-A/shot-spire-12.png

findings.text: THE VILLAGER IS A MANNEQUIN. Tessa's body and face are a genuine step up — sculpted head with a nose in profile, real dress and sleeve, red hair — and that closes the wave-4 'flat beige slab face' blocker for her. But over 3 s of burst she is essentially frozen: no breathing loop, no weight shift, no head turn, no blink, no hand animation. She does NOT face the player (strict profile the whole time, from 6 m dead in front of her), which is exactly what wave 6 claimed to have added. Her bare feet are buried in the brick garden bed and no hand is modelled where the basket hangs — the arm just ends.
findings.evidence: tools/out/V6-F/burst-vidle-0/3/6/9.png (contact sheet: identical pose), tools/out/V6-E/shot-villager.png

findings.text: THE NOON SKY IS TWO COTTON SMUDGES ON A GRADIENT. No cumulus volume, no cloud shading, no layered deck, no god rays, no crepuscular light — the bar in CLAUDE.md is explicitly 'dramatic skies with volumetric-looking clouds and god rays'. The sky is the single most-screenshotted thing in FF14 and at midday this one is emptier than a mobile game's. (Golden hour and night are the region's two genuine wins and should not be touched — the amber haze with backlit grass, and the aurora-plus-stars night, both hold up.)
findings.evidence: tools/out/V6-D/shot-noon-sky.png; contrast with tools/out/V6-D/shot-gold-vista.png and shot-night-vista.png which do work

findings.text: THE FOLIAGE IS A PICKET OF CLONES AND IT CASTS ALMOST NO SHADOW. The trees are near-identical perfectly-straight thin trunks with 3-6 sparse flat leaf clumps, spaced evenly, with zero undergrowth, bushes or ferns beneath any of them, and one comic pole-tree with a tiny crown 20 m up. At noon a full canopy throws only a few thin scribbly branch lines on the field instead of a canopy shadow, so the meadow is flat-lit with no shadow structure at all.
findings.evidence: tools/out/V6-A/shot-aeth-200.png, tools/out/V6-A/shot-hamlet-56.png, tools/out/V6-G/burst-atk-1.png

findings.text: MIRRORMERE'S SHORELINE IS THREE FLAT BANDS. A dead-straight tan sand strip, a hard cut to a solid flat green shelf, a hard cut to the treeline — no reeds, no shallows rocks, no wet-sand gradient, no waterline foam, no depth colour ramp in the water. A flat black untextured plank floats half in the water. The reflection itself is good and the ripple ring is nice; everything around it reads as a golf-course pond.
findings.evidence: tools/out/V6-F/shot-lake-settled.png, tools/out/V6-D/shot-lake.png

findings.text: GROUND COVER IGNORES BUILT SURFACES. Grass blades punch up through the Aetheryte plaza's stone deck, through the hamlet's plank decking and market counter, and through the raised brick garden beds. Nothing in FF14 or Destiny lets the terrain scatter render on top of a constructed floor.

findings.text: CREATURES OVERLAP AND IDLE STIFFLY, AND AGGRO RANGE IS SHORT. Two Aether Hounds stood inside each other's bodies with no separation steering, in an identical rigid four-legged splay across 1.5 s (only tail and head move; the legs are locked, no weight shift, no breathing). They also never closed from 30 m in open ground over ~10 s with the player standing still and firing. They DO have a real locomotion cycle when they move and the hound GLB itself is the best asset in the region — sculpted head, crystal teeth, fur shading, saturated purple that never clips — so this is animation state and steering, not the model.

findings.text: THE GOOD NEWS, stated plainly so it does not get regressed: I fought the Vale's own bestiary (2 wisps + 2 hounds at 0-2 m, plus a second fight with spawned hounds and wisps) across 40+ burst frames and NOT ONE FRAME WASHED OUT. The wisp reads as a saturated purple crystal with orbiting rune rings, the hound keeps its blue-violet, the muzzle flash does not bloom the screen. Wave 5's headline vale blob violation is genuinely closed. The Aetheryte at 40 m now has a plinth, gold rings, rune-lit inset panels, banner plates, obelisks, lantern posts and a plaza rune circle — 'greybox' is no longer a fair description at that distance. Golden hour, the night sky, the lake reflection and the region-name/minimap/haze change on the border crossing into Whisperwood all work.

gateThresholdBugs: tools/animcheck.mjs perFrame deltas are not dt-normalised and the harness launches vsync-off: measured dt alternates 5.6 <-> 9.3 ms, manufacturing a 1.6:1 alternation from frame pacing alone — exactly the signal the `alternation` test looks for. Divide each delta by that frame's dt.

outOfLaneFindings.text: An attacking hound fills 100% of the viewport — decree violation, measured. standoff clamps the ROOT to 2.2 m but the ring was tuned against procedural bodies centred on their root; the Tripo hound reaches far forward of its root. hound: standoff 2.2, minRootHoriz 2.20, minHeadBoneToCam 0.86 m. frostwolf: minAnyBoneToCam 1.06 m. The clean fix is a bodyReach measured at spawn like the existing bodyDrop, but it forces attackRange up (3.2 < 3.5) and cascades into pack pressure and bite cadence — a combat-spacing retune, left for the combat lane.

coherence.conditions: 9 harness runs, ~120 screenshots, q=high, dev server 5179. Runs shared the GPU with 13-28 other headless Chromiums from the parallel judge fleet, so no timing number is trustworthy — pixels and game state were judged, not frame times.
coherence.verdict: Cadle is a real game with a real world in it, and it is being sabotaged by three or four specific objects. The bones are better than the wave-5 verdicts suggest: ten regions with genuinely distinct light, palette and silhouette that you can walk between on foot; a parchment map and quest log that would not embarrass a shipping MMO; 55 quests whose prose is good writing, not filler; a movement core that measures Destiny-correct to the millisecond (sprint FOV kick 67.7->73.7 in 150 ms, slide boosting to 11.41 m/s, ADS 0.99 at 250 ms); a loot stream with Legendaries and power-delta arrows; and a bestiary — the gold Sentinel especially — that belongs in the same painting as the world around it. The washed-white blob decree is genuinely held: zero pixels with min-channel > 235 across every combat frame including the super. But the first thirty seconds of a fresh game wedge the player's head inside the Aetheryte's gold ring and leave them there; every region's ground within 8 m is the same flat plane with a different colour of noise on it; enemy attack VFX drown the frame in flat opaque films and one enemy bolt renders as a hard-edged solid magenta lens four metres across; and an armour drop is represented by a green t-shirt. The parts are wave-6 quality. The assembly is not.

findings.text: ~20 seconds in, holding W from spawn, your head goes inside the Aetheryte and stays there. The gold ring is a decorative torus at eye height with no collider; the collider is a cylinder around the pillar, so you are stopped by the pillar with your view buried in a featureless gold surface. This is the first thing that happens to a new player and it is an automatic-lose 'geometry you can walk into'.

findings.text: What works and must not be regressed: the unbroken 160 s walk from spawn into the Whisperwood with the minimap zone card, ground splat and haze all changing on the same step (shot-j06, shot-j12 — the best-looking frame in the game); the intro bedroom with AI posters and the gold-serif CADLE title on the monitor; the parchment map and quest log; the Aetheryte's violet stone, gold filigree and glowing rune floor; and the rigged-GLB creatures, which are better than the world they stand in.

coherence.theOneThing: Give the ground a third dimension within 15 m — in all ten regions, from one shared scatter system. Not a new texture: meshes — pebbles, grit, tufts, cracked slabs, snow crust and drift lips, ash clinker, void shards, shore wrack — instanced, ~20-30 per region, keyed off the biome id the same way BTREE/BROCK already are, and faded in over the same radius the grass uses so the grass boundary stops being a visible ring at 25 m. The Aetheryte trap is worse but it is a twenty-minute fix one builder should do today; the ground is every frame of the game, it is the fix that lifts the weakest regions most without re-authoring them, and it closes the complaint the previous coherence pass raised and that has not moved since.
